# Forwarding rule

One forwarding rule in a DNS forwarding ruleset (`Microsoft.Network/dnsForwardingRulesets/forwardingRules`):
queries for `domain_name`, from the virtual networks linked to the ruleset, go to `target_dns_servers`
through the ruleset's outbound endpoints. `modules/forwarding_ruleset` calls it once per rule; it can also
be called alone with the ruleset's resource ID.

Azure cannot change a rule's domain name, so changing it replaces the rule; targets, state and metadata
are updated in place. Azure accepts only port 53 for the targets.

Removing one metadata entry leaves the other keys as they were, and azapi compares only the keys in the
body, so the metadata is also sent through `sensitive_body`, versioned by a hash of the map: any change
is written. A plan that removes an entry shows only that version changing.

## Required Inputs

The following input variables are required:

### <a name="input_domain_name"></a> [domain\_name](#input\_domain\_name)

Description: The DNS namespace the rule forwards, dot-terminated: `contoso.com.`, or `.` for every name (a wildcard rule). One to 34 labels, or none for the wildcard. Changing it replaces the rule.

Type: `string`

### <a name="input_name"></a> [name](#input\_name)

Description: Name of the forwarding rule: letters, digits, underscores and hyphens, starting with a letter. Changing it replaces the rule.

Type: `string`

### <a name="input_parent_id"></a> [parent\_id](#input\_parent\_id)

Description: Resource ID of the DNS forwarding ruleset that holds the rule.

Type: `string`

### <a name="input_target_dns_servers"></a> [target\_dns\_servers](#input\_target\_dns\_servers)

Description: The DNS servers queries in `domain_name` are forwarded to, 1 to 6, in order: the first one answers unless it stops responding. Not Azure DNS (`168.63.129.16`), which Azure refuses as a target.

- `ip_address` - IPv4 address of the DNS server.
- `port` - (Optional) Port of the DNS server. Defaults to `53`, the only port Azure accepts ("The target DNS server port must be 53").

Type:

```hcl
list(object({
    ip_address = string
    port       = optional(number, 53)
  }))
```

## Optional Inputs

The following input variables are optional (have default values):

### <a name="input_enabled"></a> [enabled](#input\_enabled)

Description: Whether the rule is applied. A disabled rule stays in the ruleset and is ignored.

Type: `bool`

Default: `true`

### <a name="input_ignore_body_changes"></a> [ignore\_body\_changes](#input\_ignore\_body\_changes)

Description: Paths in the forwarding rule's `body` whose changes the AzAPI provider ignores. Paths use dot notation, for example `properties.metadata`. Configuration changes at an ignored path are **not** sent to Azure until that path is removed from the list.

- `network_dns_forwarding_rulesets_forwarding_rules` - Ignored body paths for the forwarding rule.

Type:

```hcl
object({
    network_dns_forwarding_rulesets_forwarding_rules = optional(list(string), [])
  })
```

Default: `{}`

## Outputs

The following outputs are exported:

### <a name="output_lock_dependency"></a> [lock\_dependency](#output\_lock\_dependency)

Description: Changes whenever the rule is created, replaced or changed. The caller passes it in the ruleset's `lock_dependencies`: Azure applies the ruleset's lock to the rule too, and a `ReadOnly` lock also blocks updating it in place, which keeps its ID.

### <a name="output_name"></a> [name](#output\_name)

Description: Name of the forwarding rule.

### <a name="output_resource_id"></a> [resource\_id](#output\_resource\_id)

Description: Resource ID of the forwarding rule.
